 Honda Recalls Over 635,000 Vehicles Over Power Steering Failures
 by 
 AutoGuide Recall Alerts 
 (IC: ) 
 Published:  November 11th, 2026 
 Share 
 Honda is issuing a safety recall for 635,808 vehicles in the United States across its Honda and Acura lineups due to a software flaw that can abruptly disable electric power steering assist while driving. 
 The campaign involves select 2023–2025 Honda Pilot crossovers, 2022–2024 Acura MDX luxury SUVs, and 2021–2025 Acura TLX sport sedans. A sudden drop in power assist substantially increases steering effort, making vehicles difficult to control at low speeds or during mid-corner maneuvers and elevating the risk of a crash.

 Software Error Triggers EPS Failsafe Mode
 According to safety recall documentation submitted to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA recall campaign number 26V721000 ), the issue stems from an internal software configuration glitch within the Electric Power Steering (EPS) control unit.
 Under certain operating conditions—such as while driving straight ahead—a calculation anomaly inside the supplier-developed code can trigger an internal system error. Rather than filtering the calculation anomaly, the EPS software is configured to respond by shifting into a failsafe mode.
 Once failsafe mode activates, electric assist cuts out immediately and warning lights illuminate on the instrument cluster. While manual steering remains mechanically intact, the sudden and dramatic increase in physical effort required to turn the wheel can catch drivers off guard.
 Honda reports that it has received 146 warranty claims related to the condition and is aware of at least one injury tied to the defect. No deaths have been reported.
 Affected Models and Population Breakdown
 The 635,808-vehicle population breaks down across three core nameplates:
 2023–2025 Honda Pilot: 383,110 units
 2022–2024 Acura MDX: 177,100 units
 2021–2025 Acura TLX: 75,598 units
 The Fix and Notification Schedule
 To remedy the issue, authorized Honda and Acura dealers will reprogram the EPS control unit with updated software free of charge.
 Owner notification letters are scheduled to be mailed beginning December 14, 2026. Affected Vehicle Identification Numbers (VINs) became searchable in the recall database on NHTSA.gov on November 11, 2026.
